experience.summary: Embedded firmware for silicon photonic integrated circuits. Now contributing to firmware for the company's next-generation product.

highlights.title: Photonics bring-up and control
points: Firmware bring-up and closed-loop control for photonic components on a CMIS-compliant ELSFP optical module.
Worked with MZI meshes, ring resonators, comb lasers, SOAs, photodiodes and TECs, with OSA measurements in the lab.
Implemented MZI tuning and calibration firmware, optical power equalization routines and thermistor-based temperature control loops.

highlights.title: Optical power monitoring
points: Developed photodiode tap ratio calibration and control, converting monitor photodiode readings into real-time optical power for closed-loop feedback.
Derived ADC/DAC conversions from PCB schematics and layout for accurate hardware interfacing.

highlights.title: Secure bootloader and field update
points: Built a secure bootloader with encrypted firmware images, enabling in-field updates over the host interface.
Implemented CMIS-standard firmware download and worked across the full update flow, from image transfer to on-device decryption and programming.

highlights.title: Data acquisition and debug
points: Developed data acquisition and debug infrastructure, including I2C data readout to Python tooling and UART logging.

experience.summary: System integration and bring-up for an autonomous racecar platform.

highlights.title: Platform bring-up
points: Led system integration and bring-up of NVIDIA Jetson and Raspberry Pi platforms for an autonomous racecar.
Validated cameras, LiDAR, motor controllers and power subsystems on a 4-layer mixed-signal PCB.
Debugged chip-level I2C, SPI and UART failures on new board builds with an oscilloscope, logic analyzer and DMM.

highlights.title: Autonomous navigation
points: Developed a ROS2 gap-following node with AprilTag-based TF lookups and Ackermann steering for closed-loop navigation.

experience.summary: Embedded Linux firmware for HMI products on multi-core ARM SoCs: profiling and latency, reproducible platform images, remote debug channels and industrial protocol validation.

highlights.title: HMI performance profiling
points: Profiled HMI runtime firmware on multi-core ARM SoCs, including Qualcomm platforms, using ftrace, perf and custom kernel-level instrumentation.
Isolated scheduling, IPC and rendering bottlenecks across the embedded Linux stack.
Drove low-level architecture decisions that cut touch-to-render latency by 15 ms (about 20%), including removing a redundant compositor sync.

highlights.title: Reproducible platform images
points: Built reproducible embedded Linux deployment images for HMI firmware across 4 hardware platforms using containerized toolchains and BSP layers.
Improved cross-platform portability of board-specific drivers, init scripts and runtime services.

highlights.title: Remote debug and display bring-up
points: Brought up secure remote debug and display channels on embedded targets by configuring Wayland/Weston compositors and VNC servers (TigerVNC, TightVNC).
Enabled over-the-network access to headless boards for firmware bring-up, validation and field debugging.

highlights.title: Protocol validation
points: Validated Modbus RTU/TCP between PLC and HMI nodes to full compliance across 3 hardware revisions.

experience.summary: Python automation and test infrastructure for network firmware configuration and multi-node hardware validation.

highlights.title: XML to CLI automation
points: Developed a Python pipeline that translates complex XML configuration data into executable CLI commands, reducing manual configuration time by 87.5%.
Engineered parsing and validation for large XML files against predefined schemas, improving validation throughput by 25%.

highlights.title: Schema-driven test framework
points: Designed and built a schema-driven unit test framework that automatically verifies and validates the generated CLI commands.

highlights.title: Integration test automation
points: Built an automated firmware integration test framework in Python and MATLAB for multi-node hardware validation, cutting regression cycles from 8 hours to under 1 hour.

experience.summary: Mechanical characterization of silicon nitride microcantilever resonators for MEMS sensing, using piezoelectric actuation and laser Doppler vibrometry.

highlights.title: Instrumentation
points: Operated an MSA-500 laser Doppler vibrometer, a vacuum microprobe station, Pfeiffer turbo pumps, and both Zurich Instruments MFLI and SRS SR844 lock-in amplifiers for precise signal detection.
Passed the facility drive test for independent access to the instruments.

highlights.title: Resonator characterization

images.caption: Measurement setup in the CeNSE lab

points: Characterized Si3N4 microcantilever resonators and identified a 430 kHz resonance frequency.
Observed resonance peak splitting at actuation voltages above 400 mV, marking the move from linear to nonlinear behavior.
Analyzed amplitude, displacement and phase against frequency in MATLAB, including 3D views across actuation voltage.

highlights.title: Outcome
points: Revealed critical nonlinear device behaviors that contributed to 2 new sensor design hypotheses for future precision-sensing R&D.
